small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_M tiles (e.g. 128/256 with BLOCK_N=128) and try num_stages=3-4 with num_warps=8; current K is tiny (72) so the kernel is output-bound and bigger M tiles amortize the bias/Mish epilogue and reduce launch grid.
- Drop the NHWC permute by writing a kernel that consumes NCHW input directly (gather per-channel with stride IH*IW) — the permute is a full read+write of the input each call and is pure overhead.
- Store output in NHWC inside the kernel and do a single permute at the end (or skip if downstream tolerant); current scatter to NCHW has strided writes of width OW that hurt coalescing across BLOCK_N.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a persistent implicit-GEMM conv where each program owns a (BLOCK_M output-pixel, BLOCK_N=OC tile) and loops over K in chunks of BLOCK_K=32; with K=72 and OC=64, fix BLOCK_N=64 and pick BLOCK_M=128-256 so one block computes a whole OC column, eliminating the pid_n dimension entirely.
- Avoid the input layout transform: index x in native NCHW by computing per-(kh,kw) base offsets outside the K-loop and stepping by IH*IW for the IC reduction; this turns the gather into contiguous IC-strided loads and removes the prologue permute (~10-15% of runtime at this size).
- Consider splitting the kernel into two passes only if shared-memory pressure forces it; otherwise keep conv+sub+Mish fused in the epilogue (already done) and ensure the Mish uses softplus = log1p(exp(min(x,20))) with the >20 fast path to keep it ~6 flops on registers.
